entry.title: Wormhole geometries in Einstein-aether theory
entry.summary: We present the first analysis of traversable wormholes within the framework of Einstein-aether theory. We show that the corresponding field equations admit three distinct wormhole geometries, obtained by adopting three different classes of combinations for the aether coupling constants. We examine the null and weak energy conditions for three types of wormhole shape functions. Our results show that, for appropriate choices of the wormhole parameters and the coupling constants of the theory, these wormhole geometries can satisfy the null and weak energy conditions. Furthermore, we find that the satisfaction of these energy conditions is restricted to certain ranges of the aether coupling constants, which can be interpreted as constraints arising from the requirement of avoiding exotic matter. However, these ranges are incompatible with the constraints imposed by physical considerations and observational bounds. This suggests that, as in Einstein gravity, exotic matter is necessary to support traversable wormhole geometries in Einstein-aether theory.

entry.title: Multi-peaked high-frequency gravitational waves from PBH-assisted leptogenesis
entry.summary: We study the possibility of probing non-thermal leptogenesis with multi-peaked high-frequency gravitational waves (GW) by considering heavy right-handed neutrino (RHN) produced from primordial black hole (PBH) evaporation to be responsible for generating the required lepton asymmetry. The decay of RHN also produces a GW spectrum due to graviton bremsstrahlung with the corresponding amplitude being enhanced for heavier RHN. The presence of an ultra-light PBH dominated epoch not only ensures sufficient production of RHNs, but also keeps the leptogenesis scenario free from strong washout problem of thermal leptogenesis at very high scale. In addition, the PBH dominated epoch also helps in generating a gravitational bremsstrahlung spectrum distinct from the stochastic GW background from the thermal bath. Finally, PBH evaporation also brings two separate sources of GW via density perturbation and graviton emission via Hawking evaporation. For the most optimistic scenario with very high scale seesaw consistent with neutrino mass and leptogenesis, this leads to a multi-peaked GW spectrum with peak frequencies lying in the MHz-EHz range.

entry.title: A Positive Turn: Coupled Quintessence and Cosmological Neutrino Masses
entry.summary: In $Λ$CDM, the CMB and DESI BAO upper limits on the total neutrino mass are in tension with the lower bounds from oscillation experiments, and analyses allowing negative effective masses favor negative values. We investigate whether a coupled quintessence (CQ) model in which dark matter interacts with a canonical scalar field $φ$ through an exponential mass coupling $m_{\rm c}(φ)\propto e^{-βφ/M_{\rm Pl}}$ can alleviate this tension. Combining CMB, DESI, and supernova data, we find that CQ yields neutrino-mass constraints comparable to those obtained in CPL and consistent with oscillation experiments within $2σ$ for normal ordering, without requiring the scalar-field equation of state to cross the phantom divide. We further show that it alleviates the tension more effectively than alternative interacting dark energy models that instead favor more negative effective masses. This comparison shows that whether dark sector interactions can relax neutrino mass bounds ultimately depends on the interplay of their effects on primary CMB anisotropies, geometry, growth, and lensing.

entry.title: Self-interacting dark matter and neutrino masses from MeV-scale lepton-number breaking
entry.summary: We show that a scalar whose vacuum expectation value (vev) breaks lepton number at the MeV scale, generating the light-neutrino masses through the inverse seesaw, can also serve as the light mediator of self-interacting dark matter. Dark matter is a pseudo-Dirac fermion whose mass splitting arises from the same vev and is predicted to be proportional to the self-interaction coupling times the vev. A strong central interaction between the dark states requires this splitting to be sizable. The CP-even mediator decays into neutrinos at a rate fixed by the neutrino masses, independent of its mixing with the Higgs boson. Fixing the coupling by the relic abundance and evaluating exact partial-wave cross sections, the model reproduces the velocity dependence of the self-interaction cross section inferred from dwarf galaxies to clusters along a narrow band, $m_s\simeq1.9~{\rm MeV}\times(m_χ/{\rm GeV})$, extending up to $m_χ\simeq12$~GeV with a best fit at $m_χ\simeq7.6$~GeV and $m_s\simeq15$~MeV, and on a sequence of resonant islands of comparable fit quality at higher masses. The cluster data bound the dark matter mass from above, so that the allowed masses extend from about $3$ to $70$~GeV ($95\%$ confidence level), with correlated mediator masses of $6$-$28$~MeV. Combining constraints from the effective number of neutrino species, SN~1987A and direct detection, we find the lepton-number-breaking scale confined to a window of a few hundred MeV and a strong preference for normal neutrino mass ordering. The allowed parameter space is testable by future measurements of $N_{\rm eff}$, low-threshold direct detection and the neutrino mass ordering.

entry.title: Two-Fluid Radial Stability of Dark-Matter-Admixed Compact Objects: Dark Compact Planets, Dark White Dwarfs, Dark Neutron Stars, and Dark Oysters
entry.summary: We investigate the equilibrium structure and stability against radial oscillations of a variety of two-fluid compact objects containing ordinary baryonic matter admixed with cold dark matter coupled through the background spacetime. For the ordinary fluid, we employ a QCD equation of state compatible with chiral effective field theory at nuclear densities (supplemented by the BPS and Negele-Vautherin models at extremely low densities) and with perturbative QCD in the high-density regime while also satisfying also current astrophysical data. For the dark fluid, we assume self-interacting fermionic matter with particle masses of $m_f=$ 2, 5, 10, and 100 GeV and two self-interaction strengths of $y=0.1$ and $10^3$. By scanning a large range of central pressures for both fluids, we identify the presence of dark compact planets, dark white dwarfs, dark neutron stars and the so-called dark oysters. Importantly, these objects are not only in two-fluid hydrostatic equilibrium, but they are also stable against two-fluid radial oscillations. We find that the relative representation of each class in the radially stable sample is strongly sensitive to the combinations of $m_f$ and $y$, with some combinations entirely suppressing some of these object classes within the sampled domain while favoring others. In addition to these classes, strong self-repulsion supports stable, dark-matter-dominated branches with compact ordinary-matter cores and extended dark halos, approaching the self-interacting fermion-star limit. Finally, we calculate the gravitational redshift at the ordinary-matter surface, $z_{\rm OM}$, including the contribution of extended dark-matter halos for which we found radially stable configurations with $z_{\rm OM}>2$.

entry.title: MAHA-z: A Mahalanobis distance kNN estimator for photometric redshifts
entry.summary: We present \texttt{MAHA-z}, a photometric-redshift (photo-$z$) estimator that combines $k$-nearest neighbour ($k$NN) regression with a Mahalanobis distance metric learned from the covariance of a spectroscopic reference sample. For each target galaxy, \texttt{MAHA-z} performs a neighbour search in a colour-magnitude feature space with optional morphological parameters, and returns both a point estimate and a redshift posterior $p(z\mid\mathbf{f})$ obtained by kernel density estimation over the neighbour redshifts. The Mahalanobis metric accounts for correlated features and heterogeneous units, eliminating ad hoc normalisation, and its subspace restriction allows \texttt{MAHA-z} to handle missing bands on a per-galaxy basis without imputation. We validate the method on four datasets spanning simulations and survey photometry: the Euclid Flagship~2 mock, the Legacy-KiDZ calibration sample, VIPERS, and the DES Year~3 BAO sample. On Euclid Flagship~2 (LSST+NISP) we achieve $σ_{\rm NMAD}=0.0148$ with a $0.27\%$ outlier fraction, and on DES Y3 we obtain $σ_{\rm NMAD}\approx0.023$ with $<1\%$ outliers and posterior calibration comparable to the \texttt{ANNz2} catalogue. \texttt{MAHA-z} processes millions of galaxies in minutes and provides competitive PDFs at substantially lower computational cost than trained machine-learning models, making it a practical option for iterative photo-$z$ production and validation in Stage-IV surveys.

entry.title: Gravitational open effective field theory of inflation
entry.summary: We construct a gravitational open extension of the effective field theory of inflation in the Schwinger-Keldysh framework. While physical symmetries allow many open operators in the Schwinger-Keldysh action, most of them overconstrain the equations of motion, yielding inconsistent dynamics. We identify a minimal open operator compatible with propagating scalar and tensor modes and build a local gravitational action, recovering known dissipative models of inflation.

entry.title: Probing soft signals of gravitational-wave memory with space-based interferometers
entry.summary: Gravitational-wave displacement memory is a remarkable, ubiquitous prediction of general relativity that has not yet been detected. Unlike the oscillatory components of gravitational waveforms, displacement memory is associated with soft gravitons and provides the leading low-frequency observable of its parent event. Analogous soft signals may also be associated with velocity and integrated-displacement memory. The simple, universal spectral shapes of soft waveforms provide effective templates for matched filtering and parameter estimation. In this paper, we investigate the detection prospects for such soft memory signals with future space-based laser interferometers. As realistic examples, we examine the infrared spectral features of gravitational waves from moderately relativistic nonspinning compact binary scattering and comparable-mass quasicircular, nonprecessing black hole mergers. In both cases, the low-frequency spectrum can be described by a soft displacement-memory waveform with finite-frequency corrections. Using the adopted instrumental-noise models, simulated Bayesian parameter-estimation analyses show that a single LISA-like detector can constrain the memory amplitude and arrival time for signals with matched-filter signal-to-noise ratios of order 10. Big Bang Observer (BBO) Stage 1 could measure null displacement memory from sufficiently loud stellar-mass compact binary mergers. We also evaluate the detectability of an idealized stochastic background of soft displacement-memory signals. These results establish gravitational-wave bursts with memory as concrete targets for space-based interferometers.

entry.title: Active learning at a graduate summer school: feasibility, student response, and the role of instructor training
entry.summary: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. We report a study at a one-week graduate school in neutrino and astroparticle physics attended by 38 students from 8 countries. Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.

entry.title: Hidden interfacial magnetism in RuO$_2$ heterostructures revealed by a superconducting spin switch
entry.summary: RuO$_2$, once the flagship altermagnetic candidate, is now believed to be nonmagnetic in the bulk, yet weak, static and spatially inhomogeneous magnetism emerges at its surfaces and interfaces. Where this magnetism resides, what stabilises it, and whether it is connected to these states remain open questions. Here we address these questions at the Nb/RuO$_2$ interface using a superconducting spin switch. A GdN/Nb/RuO$_2$ trilayer allows interfacial exchange-field alignment to tune the superconducting transition temperature of Nb, probing interfacial magnetism inaccessible to conventional magnetometry. The switch reveals a hidden magnetic subsystem, which we attribute to a thin RuO$_x$ redox layer formed as Nb scavenges oxygen from RuO$_2$. This layer behaves as a weak and magnetically hard ferromagnet with vacancy-induced anisotropy. Furthermore, supercurrent amplifies the switching efficiency, making the probe sensitivity tunable in situ. Superconducting spin switches thus emerge as a quantitative low-temperature probe of hidden magnetism at buried interfaces.

entry.title: Non-Abelian Thirring model at large $N$
entry.summary: We consider the non-Abelian bosonized Thirring model for a semi-simple group $G$ at level $k$, with deformation parameter $λ$. We compute the two-point correlation functions of current and composite current operators to cubic order in $λ$, assuming large values of the quadratic Casimir $c_G$ of the group $G$ in the adjoint representation. From these, we extract the $β$-function and the anomalous dimensions of both the current and composite current operators, showing the absence of an additional critical point of order $\frac{k}{c_G}$ to quartic order in $λ$. At this order, our findings agree with those of Destri and de Vega, but contradict the claim of Dashen and Frishman for the Fermionic non-Abelian Thirring model.

entry.title: Quasinormal overtones and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes
entry.summary: We investigate scalar quasinormal modes (QNMs), with particular attention to overtones, and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes, which interpolate between the Reissner--Nordström (RN) and Hayward limits. Over the allowed ranges of charge $q$ and regularization parameter $α_0$, all QNM frequencies have negative imaginary parts, confirming stability against scalar perturbations. Increasing either $q$ or $α_0$ can trigger overtone outbursts, with the Frolov threshold shifted to smaller parameter values than in the RN or Hayward cases. Angular momentum does not eliminate the outburst but postpones its onset from $n=1$ at $l=0$ to $n\geq 2$ at $l=1$. Comparisons of the effective potential show that, for $l=1$, charge raises the barrier peak much more strongly than $α_0$, while the clearest deviations from the Hayward and RN references are localized near the horizon. Using the QNM--grey-body correspondence at $l=1$, we find that overtone corrections are essential, and the amended formula substantially outperforms the eikonal truncation. At fixed frequency, both $q$ and $α_0$ suppress transmission, with charge being the dominant factor, consistent with the stronger barrier enhancement under the charge scan.

entry.title: The unified bound dark energy--bound dark matter model confronted with DESI DR2, ACT and SPT-3G, and the Unite supernovae measurements
entry.summary: The unified bound dark energy-bound dark matter (BDE-BDM) model derives the whole dark sector from a single supersymmetric SU(3) dark gauge group, whose lightest meson is the dark energy and whose heavier bound states, created with a velocity $v_c$ when the group condenses, are the dark matter. Because the condensation scale $Λ_c$ is fixed by gauge-coupling unification, the dark-energy sector has no free parameter beyond those of $Λ$CDM, and the dark-matter sector adds only $v_c$. We confront the model with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO), the Planck, ACT DR6 and SPT-3G D1 CMB spectra, the combined ACT and SPT CMB lensing and the Unite supernovae. The measured condensation scale, $Λ_c=43.74\pm0.11$ eV, lies inside the window $34^{+16}_{-11}$ eV predicted by unification, and the dark energy thaws without ever crossing the phantom divide, reaching $w_0=-0.9267\pm0.0003$ today; it thus reproduces the DESI distances that $w_0w_a$CDM fits with a phantom past. BDE-BDM gives the best fit to the DESI DR2 BAO of the four models, reducing $χ^2_{\rm BAO}$ by 20% with respect to $Λ$CDM, more than $w_0w_a$CDM, and over the full data combination it is statistically equivalent to both $Λ$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM, with $\ln B=-0.50$ and $-0.15$, while having two fewer dark-energy parameters than $w_0w_a$CDM. Within bound dark energy, bound dark matter is moderately preferred over cold dark matter, $\ln B=+3.2$ with $Δχ^2=-9.0$, mostly from the CMB. The data now constrain the bound velocity from both sides, $v_c=0.37\pm0.14$, which places the free-streaming cutoff of the matter power spectrum at $k_{1/2}=1.49\,h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ and lowers the amplitude of structure to $S_8=0.807\pm0.007$. Future high-redshift and Lyman-$α$ forest data, together with growth and lensing measurements, will therefore provide the decisive tests of the unified dark sector.

entry.title: Bions and infrared renormalons in Kähler sigma models with $U(1)$ isotropy
entry.summary: We study semiclassical bion contributions to the vacuum energy of Kähler sigma models with two-dimensional target spaces on $\mathbb{R} \times S^1$ with twisted boundary conditions. This is first illustrated in the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model, where explicit real and complex bion solutions are constructed in a manner analogous to that used in its quantum-mechanical reduction [1]. Evaluating the bosonic and fermionic fluctuations at one loop, we obtain the effective action with both the coupling constant and the elongation parameter properly renormalized. Integration over the bion quasi-moduli space using Lefschetz thimbles then gives the leading nonperturbative contribution, which the real and complex bion contributions cancel at the supersymmetric point, while the first imaginary ambiguity appears when deviating from the supersymmetric point. Requiring its cancellation against the perturbative ambiguity allows us to infer the corresponding infrared-renormalon pole. This is an explicit example generalizing the resurgent structure of the $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model in [2] from one coupling to two renormalized parameters. The calculation further extends to Kähler targets of one complex dimension with a $U(1)$ symmetry. At leading dilute one-loop order, the target dependence enters through the moment-map difference and the metric normalizations at the two fixed points. The ambiguity structure and infrared scaling of the bion weight are common to these targets, while the inferred pole position depends on the target metric.

entry.title: Pair localization in one-dimensional quasicrystals with spin-dependent hopping
entry.summary: We investigate the quantum localization of two interacting particles moving in a one-dimensional quasicrystal with unequal hopping amplitudes. Using a two-body Green's function approach, we determine the localization phase diagram of attractively and repulsively bound pairs, showing that increasing the hopping amplitude of one constituent while keeping the other fixed raises the critical quasiperiodic strength, promoting pair delocalization. The localization threshold nevertheless remains bounded above by the Aubry-André critical point of the slower constituent. Effective analytical descriptions capture pair localization in the limits of strong hopping imbalance and strong interactions. The dynamics of an initially on-site pair provides signatures of delocalization induced by unequal hopping amplitudes. In particular, the effective spreading exponent of the root-mean-square width of a pair distribution reveals a progression from localized to subdiffusive and eventually superdiffusive behavior as the hopping ratio increases. Our results establish unequal hopping amplitudes as a means of tuning the transport properties of interacting pairs in quasiperiodic lattices, with direct relevance to ultracold atoms in optical lattices.

entry.title: One year of broadband radio monitoring of the enigmatic transient GRB 250702B reveals the evolution of the relativistic jet
entry.summary: We present an extensive radio monitoring campaign of the unique extragalactic transient GRB 250702B, associated with unprecedentedly long duration gamma-ray emission, lasting over 3\,hr. Our observations span 0.65-233 GHz from 6-356 d (observer frame) post-discovery. The radio emission shows a smoothly evolving peaked synchrotron spectrum consistent with an adiabatic shock expanding into a stratified ambient medium ($n_e\propto R^{-k}$; $k= 1.5-2$). We detect significant variability in the low frequency ($\leq3$ GHz) light curves which we interpret as interstellar scintillation, placing an approximate bound on the blast wave image size of $1.2\times10^{16}\lesssim R_{\perp} \lesssim 5\times10^{17}$ cm. The temporal evolution of the flux density and critical synchrotron frequencies suggest the shock that powers the radio emission is potentially a wide-angle $θ_j\gtrsim15$ deg, low Lorentz factor ($Γ\lesssim10$) jet, or a narrow $θ_j\lesssim2$ deg highly relativistic jet. A narrow jet is expected for a stellar-mass black hole engine, such as a helium star merger, and the beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is consistent with the known distribution for long GRBs ($E_K\sim10^{51}$ erg). The wide-angle jet scenario would instead require a progenitor involving prolonged accretion. We derive and show an intermediate or stellar-mass black hole tidal disruption event are viable possibilities. The beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is on the low end of the known distribution for relativistic SMBH TDEs ($E_K\sim10^{50}$ erg). We disfavour an SMBH TDE due to lack of compatibility with the observed timescales. The detection of a jet shut off within the next year would favour a WD-IMBH TDE due to the shorter theoretical duration of super-Eddington accretion than the main-sequence TDE channels.

entry.title: OASIS: A Fast Dynamical Halo Finding Algorithm
entry.summary: In recent work (García et al. 2023), we advocated for defining a dynamical halo as the collection of particles that orbit their self-generated potential. Here we introduce the Orbiting-mass ASsIgnment Scheme (OASIS), a fast energy-based algorithm for constructing dynamical halo catalogs. Using single-snapshot information, OASIS achieves $\simeq 9\%$ scatter in orbiting mass estimates relative to the SPARTA particle-tracking algorithm. As an illustration of the applications enabled by OASIS, we use the Quijote and Erebos simulation suites to show that the $z=0$ dynamical halo mass function is nearly universal with respect to cosmology, and that it is well described by a modified Press-Schechter form with an effective collapse threshold $δ_{\rm sc} = 1.54$ at intermediate masses. However, this description fails at high masses.

entry.title: Helicity Decay to Baryons: The Cosmological Evolution of $L_μ-L_τ$ Gauge Fields and Baryogenesis
entry.summary: We study baryogenesis from the post-inflationary decay of helical U(1)$_{L_μ-L_τ}$ gauge fields generated during axion inflation. Assuming that Schwinger pair production is suppressed during inflation, a large helicity-to-entropy ratio $η_H$ can be generated while keeping the initial lepton asymmetry just after inflation negligible. After reheating, the dissipation of magnetic helicity sources a lepton asymmetry through the chiral anomaly, which is partially converted into a baryon asymmetry by electroweak sphaleron processes. We find that there are parameter spaces where the observed baryon asymmetry can be generated in both the turbulent and dissipation-dominated regimes of the U(1)$_{L_μ-L_τ}$ magnetic field evolution. The baryon asymmetry generation in the turbulent regime is, however, dominated by the pre-turbulent nearly frozen regime. We further find that the requirement of successful baryogenesis imposes stronger constraints on the inflationary Hubble parameter and the helicity density generated during axion inflation than the requirement for the gauge-field energy not to backreact on the inflaton dynamics.

entry.title: Field-induced magnetic quantum phase transitions in a bilayer triangular lattice antiferromagnet K$_2$Co$_2$(HPO$_3$)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)(H$_2$O)$_2$
entry.summary: We present a $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study on the spin-$1/2$ bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnet K$_2$Co$_2$(HPO$_3$)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)(H$_2$O)$_2$. Measurements were performed at temperatures down to 0.06 K and magnetic fields up to 26 T. In the field range of 0.5 T to 4 T, the low-temperature spin-lattice relaxation rate $1/T_1$ exhibits a peak, signaling the onset of a magnetically ordered state. Within this ordered phase, $1/T_1$ shows gapless behavior, suggesting a spin supersolid phase. This ordering is suppressed around 4 T. Between 6 T and 18 T, clear splittings of the NMR spectra are observed, indicating the emergence of a second ordered magnetic phase. The field derivative of the low-temperature Knight shift $K_{\rm n}$ reveals changes in slope at approximately 10 T, 15.5 T, and 18 T. The first two features correspond to bulk magnetizations of $1/3$ and $2/3$ of the fully saturated moment, respectively, while the last one marks a quantum phase transition from the second ordered phase to the fully polarized state. These results establish the studied compound as a platform for investigating field-induced quantum phase transitions and emergent phases in frustrated bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnets.

entry.title: Investigating production of TeV-scale muons in extensive air shower at 2400 m underground
entry.summary: Deep underground experiments present a new avenue to probe the first interactions in extensive air showers or hadronic interactions in the extreme forward phase space. The China Jinping Underground Laboratory, characterized by a vertical rock overburden of 2,400 m, provides an exceptionally effective shield against cosmic muons with energies below 3 TeV. The surviving high-energy muons, produced in the first interactions of extensive air showers, open a unique observational window into primary cosmic rays from tens of TeV up to the PeV scale and beyond. This distinctive feature also enables detailed studies of charged hadron production in the earliest stages of shower development. Using 1,338.6 live days of data collected with a one-ton prototype detector for the Jinping Neutrino Experiment, we measured the underground muon flux originating from air showers. The results show discrepancies of about 40% corresponding to significances of more than 2$σ$, relative to predictions from several leading hadronic interaction models. We interpret these findings from two complementary perspectives: (i) by adopting the expected cosmic-ray spectra, we constrain the modeling of the first hadronic interactions in air showers and provide novel insights into resolving the long-standing muon puzzle; and (ii) by assuming specific hadronic interaction models, we infer the mass composition of cosmic rays, and our data favor a lighter component in the corresponding energy range. Our study demonstrates the potential of deep underground laboratories to provide new experimental insights into air shower physics and cosmic rays.

entry.title: AGN feedback destroying group cool cores --- a case study on IC 2476 with a remnant radio AGN and an exceptionally low abundance
entry.summary: We present results from deep XMM-Newton observations ($\sim$180 ksec) of the galaxy group IC 2476 in the X-GAP sample, capturing a rare AGN feedback regime, where the central radio AGN has ceased activity but the radio lobes are still detectable. The hot intragroup medium of IC 2476 features a compact cool core, with a size of ~10 kpc, and a moderate X-ray luminosity of $\sim3.4\times10^{40}$ erg/s. We measured an unusually low temperature of $\sim$0.45 keV within the cool core. We measured an exceptionally low abundance of below ~0.2 solar, even in the central region. The X-ray surface brightness of the group is not symmetric and shows a clear depression in the region overlaid with the eastern radio lobe, suggesting the presence of an X-ray cavity. The scaled entropy of the hot gas within 0.1 r500 of IC 2476 is among the highest in X-ray galaxy groups with a similar system temperature. Our study suggests that the past powerful radio AGN outburst in IC 2476 has disrupted the cool core and the X-ray cavity has dissipated or mixed with the surrounding hot gas since the shutdown of the central AGN. A large cool core may be gradually re-established in the absence of AGN activity. This system therefore provides a great example of AGN feedback destroying the group cool core, even with a moderate radio luminosity at present.

entry.title: Rare-earth oxysulfides RE$_2$O$_2$S as model mixed-anion frustrated magnets
entry.summary: The study of low-dimensional and anisotropic magnetism is a promising avenue for the discovery of novel quantum phenomena. Mixed-anion materials, defined by the coordination of metal cations by two or more distinct anionic species, provide an intrinsically anisotropic platform for the tuning of structural, magnetic, and electronic properties. In this work, we report the synthesis and characterization of a family of rare-earth oxysulfide (RE$_2$O$_2$S) antiferromagnets (AFM) possessing a triangular-bilayer slab lattice geometry. Transitions consistent with long-range AFM order are observed for the majority of compositions, with several (RE = Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm) having been previously unreported. Although assumed to form stoichiometrically, pair distribution function (PDF) analysis provides evidence for significant, synthesis-dependent interslab structural disorder as RE$_2$O$_{2+x}$S$_{1-x}$, resulting in significant variability in the bulk magnetic response of the Nd member. This work highlights the tunability of frustrated magnetic ground states in rare-earth-based mixed-anion materials, and the importance of thorough structural characterization in the discovery of new mixed-anion magnets.

entry.title: Boundary dualities of symplectic Chern-Simons theories and minimal models
entry.summary: We propose that a Neumann-type boundary condition of the 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ $USp(2n)$ Chern-Simons theory at the level $-(n+\frac32)$ with a fundamental chiral multiplet is dual to a Dirichlet-type boundary condition of an Abelian rank-$0$ theory. In a topological twist we propose that it supports the affine vertex operator algebra (VOA) $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2))$. With the corresponding specialization of the fugacities, the line defect half-indices of the antisymmetric Wilson lines give, up to monomials, the supercharacters of all its modules, which coincide up to signs with the characters of the Virasoro minimal model $M(2,2n+3)$. We extend the duality to the level $-(n+\ell+\frac12)$ and propose that the boundary VOA is $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2\ell))$. Together with the Giveon-Kutasov type duality and the mirror symmetry, the proposed dualities form a web of dualities of the boundary conditions and the line operators. For other gauge groups with real matter we propose that the boundary VOA in the holomorphic twist is the commutant of the gauge currents in free real fermions, which is the Ising model for $Spin(7)$ with the spinor and the $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal minimal model $SM(3,5)$ for $G_2$ with $\mathbf7$.

entry.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
entry.summary: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are described by second-order tensor perturbations that contain free radiation together with a gauge-dependent response maintained by the scalar source. For a perfect fluid with constant equation of state $0<w<1$, we identify the free radiation with the out-state of the tensor perturbation, assembled from the light-cone residue of kernel functions for each pair of scalar modes. Its amplitudes follow from a classical LSZ-type reduction formula, in terms of the initial data and the light-cone-projected source. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: a redefinition of the tensor perturbation whose late-time shift has power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leaves these amplitudes unchanged. Transformations between intrinsic gauges, whose slice-normal observers and spatial coordinates are fixed by the matter and geometry without an external clock or independent oscillatory dynamics, are redefinitions of this kind, except on resonance surfaces of zero measure. The out-state is therefore the same in all intrinsic gauges, including the standard gauges of cosmological perturbation theory. The late-time Newtonian kernel is then the out-state kernel, which justifies its use for the energy spectrum of the free radiation. In matter domination, the out-state instead separates the free radiation from the static tidal response.

entry.title: Differential Monodromy, $q$-Opers, and Universal $(G,q)$-Wronskians
entry.summary: We give a geometric formulation of the $q$DE/ODE/IM correspondence for families of differential operators associated with simple Lie algebras of ADE type. Under analytic hypotheses, the $q$-connection associated with shifted monodromy defines a twisted $(G,q)$-oper and has Steinberg form in the frame of solutions normalized by prescribed asymptotics in a sector at infinity. We identify the central connection between the normalized solution frames at zero and infinity with a universal meromorphic $(G,q)$-Wronskian. Its generalized minors give $Q$-functions satisfying the ADE $QQ$-relations. When $q$ is not a root of unity, we parametrize shifted monodromy by quantum-affine $q$-characters evaluated on shifted $Q$-ratios, using the same character formulas that describe normalized transfer-matrix eigenvalues. We verify the analytic hypotheses for generic untwisted Feigin--Frenkel--Hernandez affine opers, thereby relating these affine opers to twisted $(G,q)$-opers.

entry.title: Giant Graviton Correlators: From Non-maximal to Dual, Bootstrap and Hidden Symmetry
entry.summary: We compute four-point functions of two light $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS operators and two heavy giant graviton operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills theory at large $N$ and infinite 't Hooft coupling. Using bootstrap techniques, we determine the correlators for arbitrary light-operator dimensions and arbitrary allowed sizes of non-maximal sphere and dual giant gravitons. We show that these correlators exhibit a hidden ten-dimensional conformal symmetry, allowing them to be organized into compact generating functions. Remarkably, the generating functions for both types of giant gravitons can be obtained from the maximal giant case through $SO(2,10)$ rotations in the embedding space.

entry.title: Impact on Inferred Neutron Star Equation of State due to Nonlinear Hydrodynamics, Background Spin, and Relativity
entry.summary: Tidal interaction is a unique, detectable signature in gravitational wave signals from inspiraling binary neutron stars (BNSs), which can be used to constrain the neutron star (NS) equation of state (EoS). The tidal interaction is resonantly amplified as the orbital frequency approaches the NS fundamental mode (f-mode) frequency. It has been shown that the exclusion of tidal resonance in parameter estimation leads to a significant bias in the inferred NS tidal deformability and hence the NS EoS [Pratten et al. PRL 129, 081102 (2022)]. The strength and location of tidal resonance depend sensitively on the f-mode frequency, which is typically modeled using its universal relation with the tidal deformability that is derived for an isolated, non-spinning NS assuming only linear fluid perturbations. In a BNS inspiral, the f-mode frequency can be corrected by at least three known effects: nonlinear hydrodynamics, background spin, and relativity. We use Hamiltonian Monte Carlo simulations to estimate the systematic bias on tidal deformability when each frequency correction is ignored. Our study considers both loud, individual events and the stacking of a population of detections. Both scenarios are expected when the next-generation detectors are available with a sensitivity level increased by about an order of magnitude.
entry.arxiv:journal_ref: Classical and Quantum Gravity, Volume 43, Number 12, Pages 125011, 2026

entry.title: A dual-moment framework toward unification of the four fundamental interactions
entry.summary: The unification of the four fundamental interactions remains one of the central open challenges in fundamental physics. Most existing unification scenarios rely on extra spatial dimensions, novel symmetry structures, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. In this work, we construct a minimal phenomenological dual-moment framework rooted in primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently described within a unified inverse-square-law formalism. We postulate a universal coupling relation $T = Z/c^2$ that connects source-charge coupling coefficients and moment-mediated coupling coefficients across different interaction sectors. While the framework can formally accommodate weak-charge degrees of freedom, full quantitative computations for weak-interaction dynamics are deferred to future follow-up studies. The model reproduces established low-energy dynamical limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons, and predicts distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects. We further design three independent test schemes: improved torsion-balance measurements, a mass-current laboratory deflection experiment, and astronomical light-bending observations. Although laboratory measurements impose formidable technical challenges, astronomical observations of compact spinning objects offer promising avenues to constrain or falsify the proposed framework.
entry.arxiv:comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, submitted to Physical Review D. A classical unified framework for four fundamental interactions, with gravitational lensing and torsion balance tests

entry.title: Thermal $CP$ dynamics in a four-fermion model: mean-field and functional renormalization group analyses
entry.summary: We investigate a one-flavor four-fermion model with scalar, pseudoscalar, and mixed scalar-pseudoscalar interactions at finite temperature and vanishing chemical potential. Our analysis combines the mean-field approximation, which determines the equilibrium condensates, with the functional renormalization group (FRG), which describes the scale dependence of the interactions and the fermion mass phase. Within the mean-field approach, we find that, in the absence of explicit symmetry-breaking sources, the dominant interaction determines the direction of condensation. In particular, a pseudoscalar condensate spontaneously breaks the ordinary $P/CP$ symmetry and disappears through a continuous thermal phase transition. For regular high-temperature FRG trajectories, the dimensionless mixed coupling tends to zero in the infrared, while its dimensionful counterpart remains finite. Increasing temperature also suppresses the scale evolution of the fermion mass phase. Together, these results clarify the distinct roles of thermal fluctuations in suppressing spontaneous symmetry breaking and fermionic instabilities, without necessarily eliminating explicit symmetry breaking effects.

entry.title: Identification of the C IV $λλ$5801, 5812 Emission in the Off-Nuclear TDE 2025abcr
entry.summary: TDE 2025abcr is a tidal disruption event (TDE) located approximately 9 kpc in projection from its host galaxy nucleus. Our spectroscopic follow-up with the Very Large Telescope (VLT) reveals C IV $λ\lambda5801, 5812$ emission, representing the first identification of this C IV doublet in a TDE. These transitions are uncommon in active galactic nuclei (AGN) spectra but have been observed in supernova flash spectra and Wolf-Rayet (WR) stars. We propose that the doublet arises from the combined effects of continuum fluorescence and photon trapping in the 312 Å transition, analogous to the mechanism operating in nitrogen-sequence Wolf-Rayet (WN) winds. This mechanism requires intense extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) illumination and a high optical depth, providing a distinctive diagnostic of the physical conditions in optically thick TDE outflows. These requirements, together with the relatively narrow widths of the broad emission lines, the presence of Bowen fluorescence features, and the small inferred blackbody radius, favor a compact and dense envelope in TDE 2025abcr. The optical C IV doublet may have been overlooked in previous observational and theoretical studies of TDEs, motivating more detailed radiative-transfer calculations for optically thick outflows. With future TDE samples from Rubin/LSST and WFST, a larger C IV TDE sample will test if this population systematically favors a compact photosphere.

entry.title: A Perspective on Topological Charge Density Wave Materials
entry.summary: Charge density waves are among the earliest known ordered states in quantum materials, yet they have re-emerged at the center of modern discussions of topology, symmetry breaking, and collective dynamics. In several material classes, charge-density-wave order reshapes electronic bands, boundary states, defect structures, and electromagnetic responses in ways that invite a topological interpretation. Real-space imaging has shown that incommensurate order can form networks of phase defects rather than uniform modulations. Boundary-resolved spectroscopy has revealed in-gap modes whose existence and spatial structure track the charge-density-wave order, although such observations remain confined to a single material family. In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. In kagome metals, charge order is intertwined with Berry curvature, unconventional symmetry breaking, and superconductivity. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially. This Perspective traces the development of these ideas, clarifies the evidence behind each class, identifies unresolved questions and points of debate, and outlines experimental criteria for establishing topology in charge-density-wave states.
entry.arxiv:comment: Perspective article. 36 pages, 7 figures, 1 table, 180 references. Submitted to Applied Physics Reviews

entry.title: Early--Narrow and Late--Wide Populations of GRB X-ray Flares
entry.summary: The physical origin of gamma-ray burst (GRB) X-ray flares remains debated, particularly whether they arise from prolonged central-engine activity or from variability in the external shock. Building on our previous analysis of 89 Swift GRBs with measured redshifts, we investigate the rest-frame temporal properties of X-ray flares detected in 61 bursts. We apply a multivariate Gaussian Mixture Model to rest-frame peak times and widths. We identify two statistically distinct populations: early-narrow flares (80%), with characteristic peak times of approximately 10^2 s and w/t_pk <= 1, and late-wide flares (20%), with characteristic peak times of ~ 10^3.5 s and w/t_pk >= 2. Of the 61 single or first flares, 55 belong to the early-narrow population and only 6 to the late-wide population. Of the 36 second flares, 23 (64%) belong to the early-narrow population, with shorter waiting times, whereas 13 (36%) belong to the late-wide population, with substantially longer waiting times. The width-peak-time correlation remains significant for early-narrow flares but not for late-wide flares. Furthermore, we find no correlation between flare width and energy. We find a decline of flare luminosity with peak time, driven primarily by the early-narrow population, but not statistically significant for late-wide flares. These results imply that a simple shift in time, potentially associated with later episodes of central-engine activity, cannot explain the distinction between the two flare populations. On the other hand, the peak times are consistent with expectations from an accretion disk formed following the collapse of a stellar-size massive star. Combined with our previous finding that flare properties are independent of the presence of an X-ray plateau, these results favor prolonged accretion-driven central-engine activity over external-shock variability as the primary origin of X-ray flares.

entry.title: Millimeter-Wavelength Constraints on Circular Polarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background at Arcminute Scales with the Simons Array
entry.summary: We present constraints on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) circular polarization anisotropy at arcminute angular scales, using dedicated measurements from the Simons Array taken with a quarter-wave plate and rotating half-wave plate. A detection of circular polarization in the CMB would probe a range of proposed generation mechanisms, from Standard Model astrophysics to physics beyond it. At an observing frequency of 90 GHz, we place constraints over the multipole range $300 \leq \ell \leq 2000$, corresponding to angular scales of 5.4-36 arcmin, in bands of width $Δ\ell = 100$, roughly tripling the highest multipole previously reached by a $V$-mode power spectrum measurement. Within this domain, we constrain the 95% confidence upper bound of $\ell (\ell+1) C_\ell^{VV} / (2π)$ to range from ${\sim}22\,μ\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 350$ bandpower to ${\sim}3.5\times10^3\,μ\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 1950$ bandpower. These limits are derived from ${\sim}2.5$ months of observations of each of two small regions of the sky located away from the Galactic plane, totaling ${\sim}12\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ of effective sky area. Because the methodology of this study marginalizes known foreground contamination, these bounds serve as robust, conservative limits on the true CMB circular polarization signal down to the sensitivity limits of the instrument. Additionally, we provide an experimental and analytical framework for implementing circular polarization observations on other telescopes by utilizing a quarter-wave plate and half-wave plate design.
entry.arxiv:comment: 32 pages, 14 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to ApJ

entry.title: High Precision Fundamental Physics Experiments at JLab with Spin-transparent Storage Rings of Low-energy Polarized Electron Beams
entry.summary: A breakthrough in fundamental physics experiments measuring particle spin precession may happen if spin-transparent storage rings become adopted tools for such experiments. We present a new design of highly specialized table-sized storage rings, which use low-energy polarized electron beams and Mott polarimetry. Based on the spin transparency ansatz, the spin precession stemming from the magnetic dipole moment is canceled at any beam energy after an electron's turn along the periodic orbit in the ring. Meanwhile, a spin precession induced by the fundamental physics of interest, e.g., the electron's permanent electric dipole moment (EDM) and/or ultralight-dark-matter-mediated forces such as axions, will accumulate. However, capitalizing on such types of rings is not only desirable for measurements of EDMs and axion searches relevant to $CP$ violation and matter-antimatter asymmetry in the Universe, but may also find very promising applications in quantum computing.

entry.title: Low-mass failed supernovae and the $10\,M_{\odot}$ peak in the merging black hole mass distribution
entry.summary: Gravitational-wave observations reveal that the rate of merging black holes drops by $\sim2$ orders of magnitude from component masses $\sim 10\,M_{\odot}$ to $\sim 15\,M_{\odot}$. The increased compactness of the black hole progenitor cores may contribute to the $\sim 10\,M_{\odot}$ overdensity, but cannot fully explain the rate difference. In this paper, we consider the possibility that the overdensity is reinforced by supernova processes that result in efficient black hole formation from direct collapse in a narrow range around $10\, M_{\odot}$. We extend previous studies by considering a distinct subpopulation of failed-supernovae black holes, possibly separated by a gap in the primary mass distribution from the rest of the population. Using 153 observations from the latest GWTC-4.0 catalog, we confirm a strong peak in the primary mass distribution at $10\,M_{\odot}$, with a peak rate density of $7.36_{-3.11}^{+6.35}$ $M_{\odot}^{-1}\mathrm{yr}^{-1} \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}$. The rate drops sharply and becomes consistent with zero at the 90 % level for primary mass $m_1\in (12.0, 16.1)\, M_{\odot}$, then rises again to confidently nonzero values above $\sim 16\,M_{\odot}$ before falling at higher masses. Our results reveal structure in the mass distribution in the $10-20\,M_{\odot}$ range, with rate changes of multiple orders of magnitude across a few solar masses, consistent with a distinct population of failed-supernova black holes. These conclusions persist in the latest GWTC-5.0 catalog.

entry.title: 0.5 eV QCD Axion Cosmology
entry.summary: The best available determination of the present expansion rate of the universe using late-universe observations, by the SH0ES collaboration in 2025, differs by more than seven standard deviations from the value of the Hubble constant determined by the Planck collaboration in 2018 using early-universe observations and the standard cold dark matter cosmology with cosmological constant, a discrepancy known as the Hubble tension. Within a spatially flat, isotropic, and homogeneous expanding-universe solution of the field equations of general relativity with cosmological constant, the SH0ES value for the Hubble constant implies roughly twice as many baryons as the standard cosmology, provided that one retains the Planck values for the energy density of cold dark matter in the present universe and for the cosmological constant. A novel cosmology is proposed --- in terms of cooling dark matter made of quantum chromodynamic (QCD) axions with present number density six times that of the photons in the cosmic microwave background --- which realizes this straightforward, doubled-baryons scenario for resolving the Hubble tension.
entry.arxiv:comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, now with determination of strong coupling constant to 1.3 ppm

entry.title: Viscosity heats, diffusion drains: Open-system thermodynamics in unimodular cosmology
entry.summary: In GR with bulk viscosity and in unimodular gravity with energy diffusion, the matter sector is non-adiabatic, and their balance, entropy, and temperature equations match if $Π\leftrightarrow \dot{Q}/3H$. Disagreement over whether unimodular cosmology is adiabatic comes from assigning entropy to matter only or to the total effective fluid. The key is the temperature $T_D$ of the sector absorbing the diffused energy: comoving entropy production is $\dot{Q}(1/T_D-1/T_m)$, yielding earlier limits for $T_D \rightarrow \infty$ and $T_D \rightarrow T_m$. For finite $T_D$, diffusion acts like heat exchange with an external reservoir: unlike viscosity, which only heats a closed fluid, diffusion into a colder bath can cool an open one, breaking the viscosity-diffusion correspondence for observables and stability. Cosmographically, $Π$ is fixed by the deceleration $q$, while diffusion is fixed by the jerk $j$; thus $Λ$CDM is the adiabatic limit of unimodular cosmology but remains dissipative when modeled via viscosity. The diffusive analogue of $|Π|/ρ$ is the shift $c_s^2-ω$ in effective sound speed, set by perturbative stability rather than acceleration. If dark matter is a gas with conserved rest mass, consistent diffusion removes only thermal energy, forbids phantom behavior, and bounds the growth of the cosmological term by the finite thermal reservoir; producing a logotropic dark fluid with conserved particle number would require relativistic dark matter at $z\simeq12$. With the Hayward-Kodama apparent-horizon temperature, the generalized second law in unimodular gravity follows from the local one, whereas for bulk viscosity it must be imposed separately.

entry.title: Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes
entry.summary: Understanding when gravitational collapse produces a black hole remains a central challenge in general relativity. Black-hole uniqueness results characterize the stationary endpoint under suitable assumptions, while singularity theorems establish geodesic incompleteness in the presence of trapped surfaces and appropriate energy and global conditions. Neither, however, provides a general criterion for horizon formation. The hoop conjecture offers such a criterion by relating the enclosed mass to the compactness of a matter distribution in every direction. We construct axisymmetric families of initial data describing rotating dust and test a formulation of the conjecture adapted to this setting. We explore highly prolate and oblate configurations with both constant and differential rescaled angular-velocity profiles, including configurations near the threshold for apparent-horizon formation. We find that the conjecture holds for rotating configurations, with a coefficient within 14% of unity as in the nonrotating case, provided the quasilocal mass includes the rotational energy. If the irreducible mass of the apparent horizon is used instead, the deviations grow with spin, as they do for Kerr black holes. For horizonless configurations, the conjecture likewise holds when the mass is restricted to the energy enclosed by the matter surface, whereas using the ADM mass, which also includes rotational field energy outside the matter, leads to apparent violations of up to $\approx$25%. We also discuss the possible evolution of compact configurations without apparent horizons, their relation to weak cosmic censorship, and their implications for horizonless compact objects.

entry.title: Expiscating the black hole singularity in holography
entry.summary: We argue that the leading exponential rate in the high frequency asymptotics of holographic thermal two-point functions is independent of the conformal dimension and spin (held fixed) of the operator. We analyze the leading universal WKB spectral curve governing the asymptotics at non-vanishing momentum scaling with frequency. We show that its classical action governs time domain signatures of the bouncing geodesic singularity, highly damped quasinormal modes, and the asymptotics of multi-stress tensor OPE coefficients. Beyond the leading order, we examine linear and dimension-dependent sublinear scalings of momentum with frequency. In both regimes, we derive the connection matrix between the boundary and the horizon using exact-WKB techniques. The results show a factorization of the spectral function into a perturbative part controlled by the OPE and a non-perturbative part governed by WKB transport. For linear scaling at fixed $k/ω$ in the timelike regime, the turning points controlling physical transport remain separated from the curvature singularity. Nevertheless, a singularity-anchored representative of the same transport homology class determines the leading WKB action. In the sublinear regime, the relevant turning points approach the singularity. We match an exact solution of the near-singularity scaled equation to the exterior WKB solution to determine the connection matrix and spectral function. Our results clarify how the black hole curvature singularity is encoded in dual field theory observables at leading order in the planar expansion.

entry.title: Polarized Equatorial Emission around Kerr Black Holes with Synchronized Scalar Hair. II. Indirect images
entry.summary: We investigate the intensity polarization properties of the indirect images of a geometrically and optically thin accretion disk around fully self-consistent models of Kerr black holes with synchronized scalar hair. The presence of a massive, self-gravitating scalar field can dramatically alter the lensing properties of the spacetime, resulting in morphologically complex indirect images. We show that for a representative high scalar charge model, this results in the presence of high order central ring-like images at low observer inclinations. These images are not exponentially demagnified, and their polarized intensity, relative to the direct images, is significant. We therefore conclude that the observational signature of strongly scalarized Kerr black holes may not be dominated solely by the $n=1$ image, as images with $n\geq2$ may also contribute significantly to the observed polarized emission, depending on the radial emissivity profile of the disk and the observer inclination.

entry.title: Detectability of Seyfert galaxies in point-source and stacking searches with a global network of neutrino telescopes
entry.summary: Recent evidence for high-energy neutrino emission from NGC 1068 and other nearby Seyfert galaxies suggests that active galactic nuclei (AGNs) may constitute a class of astrophysical neutrino sources. Using a physically motivated neutrino emission model based on stochastic particle acceleration in magnetized AGN coronae, we investigate the detection prospects of X-ray-bright Seyfert galaxies with a detector network comprising IceCube, Baikal-GVD, KM3NeT/ARCA, and P-ONE. We find that the Circinus Galaxy is the most promising point-source target in the Southern sky and will be detected at the 5$σ$ level by 2038 at the latest, provided that the Seyfert population accounts for the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux up to 100 TeV and Circinus is at least as efficient a neutrino emitter as the average source in the population. Individual detections of other nearby Seyferts are expected to remain challenging, making stacking searches informed by X-ray observations the most promising approach for discovering them within the next decade. Our results demonstrate that joint analyses across multiple neutrino telescopes, together with future MeV gamma-ray observations, will be essential for establishing Seyfert galaxies as astrophysical neutrino sources and provide a means for testing the coronal origin of their neutrino emission.

entry.title: Neutron Scattering studies of the density dependence of One-dimensional Quantum Fluids
entry.summary: In previous work, we demonstrated that $^4$He confined within a templated porous material preplated with a noble gas to enhance dimensional reduction exhibits one-dimensional behavior. Neutron scattering revealed that the excitations in confined $^4$He are qualitatively distinct from those in two- and three-dimensional superfluid helium, aligning with quantum Monte Carlo calculations. These simulations suggest that three solid layers form, with a one-dimensional liquid located at the center of the pore. Here, we present neutron scattering results as the filling fraction of the one-dimensional core is varied. We observe that the one-dimensional liquid always forms with a fixed density, even as the pore filling increases. We posit that this is due to the growth of the one dimensional extent of the liquid as the filling is increased, but its density remains unchanged.

entry.title: Fermi gas of polar molecules in the Pauli-blocked regime
entry.summary: Quantum gases of polar molecules have recently emerged as a powerful platform for exploring exotic many-body dynamics and correlated quantum behavior. To achieve the full potential of this platform, the production of deeply degenerate quantum gases of molecules in arbitrary confinement geometries is necessary. Here, we successfully evaporate fermionic KRb molecules in both 3D and quasi-2D geometries to well below their Fermi temperatures utilizing dipolar collisions. As we evaporate deeper into degeneracy in both geometries, we enter the Pauli-blocked regime with polar molecules, which we independently confirm by measuring the Pauli suppression of elastic collisions. Moreover, the Pauli suppression of collisions contributes to the limitation of our final molecular temperature to about 25% of the Fermi temperature in both geometries, particularly limiting quasi-2D evaporation where the Pauli blockade drastically reduces an otherwise large elastic to inelastic scattering ratio. This work demonstrates the production of degenerate Fermi gases of polar molecules both in a 3D harmonic trap and in mono- and bi-layer 2D configurations. Further, our work explores the fundamental limits on evaporation of molecular Fermi gases set by the Pauli-exclusion principle, which could be overcome in the future by introducing distinguishable scattering partners.

entry.title: Beyond Self-Similarity: Reconciling X-Ray Scaling Relations in Galaxy Clusters and Groups
entry.summary: Scaling relations hold among observed quantities that describe the thermodynamic properties of the gas in galaxy clusters and groups. However, observed data show systematic departures from the self-similar model's baseline predictions, particularly in lower-mass systems. I show that the observed departures from self-similar predictions can be efficiently described by two physical quantities modeled with power laws: the gas mass fraction $f_g$ and the temperature variation $f_T$. Using a wide range of published X-ray scaling relations, this study conducts an MCMC-based meta-analysis to constrain the temperature- and redshift-dependence of the meta-parameters $f_g$ and $f_T$ and calibrate the model. These calibrations indicate that, while the gas mass fraction does not show significant evolution with cosmic time, it decreases significantly with decreasing halo mass. On the other hand, the temperature variation shows a mild positive increase with both mass and redshift. Overall, modeling the departures from the self-similar model with $\{f_g, f_T\}$ drastically improves predictive accuracy, reducing the number of scaling relations in $>3σ$ ($>5 σ$) tension from 49 (36) percent under the self-similar scenario to just 11 (3) percent (four and one out of 39, respectively) that might be identified for their peculiarity. Moreover, modeling through this generalized framework allows for an extended discussion of the expected slopes and redshift evolution for several X-ray scaling laws, including the new quantity $Y_{LGT0} = L^{-1} M_g^2 T^{a_L}$, a proxy for the cluster's volume that is independent of $f_g$ and $f_T$ by construction, and is predicted to scale directly with mass with a well-defined redshift evolution ($M \sim Y_{LGT0} f_g^0 f_T^0 E_z^2$), as validated against hydrodynamical simulations and observational constraints.
entry.arxiv:comment: 8 pages (plus 2 pages of Appendix). A&A in press. This revised version includes a new subsection (Sect. 2.1) on the mass proxy Y_{LGT0}}, which has been corrected, and an extended analysis of the systematic uncertainties associated with the estimation of the meta-parameters

entry.title: Constraints on Complex Electroweak WIMPs from Solar Capture
entry.summary: One of the most convincing realizations of particle dark matter is provided by models based on electroweak multiplets. The lightest neutral state of such a multiplet can be a stable Majorana fermion or a real scalar, and its phenomenology is governed by two parameters: the dark matter mass and the mass splitting $\{m_χ,δ\}$. The sub-MeV range for $δ$ is particularly important as it allows for a large inelastic scattering cross section. In this paper, we analyze solar capture, energy loss, and annihilation of scalar and fermionic electroweak multiplet dark matter, generalizing earlier results for the Higgsino to other representations. We find that, while the case of a doublet is somewhat special, higher representations behave in a self-similar way. For the higher multiplets, IceCube results constrain the splitting to $δ\gtrsim 350$ keV for all dark matter masses up to $100$ TeV. Assuming thermal freeze-out and a Standard Halo Model velocity distribution, this rules out most models of electroweak dark matter as a possible origin of the single high-recoil event reported by the LZ collaboration. We also show that a high-velocity tail in the dark matter distribution, such as that induced by the Large Magellanic Cloud, raises the splitting preferred by the LZ event above the solar bounds for many of the multiplets.
entry.arxiv:comment: 11 pages, 4 figures. Updated figures with improved numerical resolution; added results and discussion for loop-induced spin-independent scattering in the electroweak doublet cases

entry.title: Eccentricity greatly enhances the detectability of line-of-sight acceleration in gravitational wave signals
entry.summary: Compact object binaries formed dynamically are characterized by a tail of eccentric sources and by the potential presence of environmental perturbations. Here we show that the presence of eccentricity in a gravitational-wave (GW) signal strongly enhances the sensitivity to environmental effects, focusing in particular on line-of-sight acceleration (LSA). We demonstrate that this enhancement is recovered in Fisher-analysis forecasts and, crucially, persists in full Bayesian parameter estimation using state-of-the-art eccentric waveform models. The key insight is that the signal should be analyzed from the moment the first detectable eccentric harmonic enters the detector band, rather than from the customary entry of the $n=2$ harmonic: this allows to probe the early inspiral and thus a longer signal, over which the GW dephasing introduced by LSA becomes substantially larger. We show that with this approach constraints on LSA can increase by more than an order of magnitude between eccentricities at 20~Hz $e_{20}=0$ and $e_{20}\sim0.1$, for signals with sufficient signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR), while we predict a factor $5$ amplification even for low-SNR ones. Fully exploiting this effect necessitates the continued improvement of efficient eccentric waveform models and likelihood evaluations, enabling the efficient analysis of signals lasting thousands of seconds and containing a large number of harmonics.

entry.title: TITAN DR1: The Type Ia Supernova Trove from ATLAS in the Nearby Universe - Host Galaxies I: Associations, Redshifts and Derived Properties
entry.summary: We present the host-galaxy catalogue for TITAN DR1, a sample of 8378 spectroscopically confirmed Type Ia supernovae (SNe~Ia) at $z \lesssim 0.15$ -- the largest homogeneous low-redshift SN Ia sample assembled to date. We describe the association of each SN with its host, the compilation of redshifts, measurements of uniform far-ultraviolet to mid-infrared (FUV--MIR) photometry, and the derivation of host properties through spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting. Combining four host-association methods with manual vetting, we securely identify hosts for 7856 SNe~Ia (93.8\%). We compile host-galaxy spectroscopic redshifts for 5522 objects and provide CMB-frame and peculiar-velocity-corrected redshifts. \rev{PSF-matched} photometry is measured for 7568 host galaxies, including both global fluxes and local optical-only fluxes within a fixed 1.5~kpc aperture centred on the SN; \texttt{Bagpipes} returns successful global fits for \rev{all} hosts and local fits for 7329. Stellar mass and rest-frame $g-z$ colour are robustly measured from optical data alone, whereas reliable estimates of star-formation rate, dust attenuation, and mass-weighted age require broader wavelength coverage to break age--dust degeneracies\rev{, and are reported for 5827 hosts}; in our redshift range, MIR data suffice and far-IR coverage is not required. The hosts span a representative low-redshift galaxy population, with a median stellar mass of $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)=10.22$ (\rev{60\%} high-mass; $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)>10$), \rev{71\%} star-forming ($\log_{10}(\mathrm{sSFR}/\mathrm{yr}^{-1}) > -10.5$), and an approximately exponential $A_V$ distribution. This catalogue provides the foundation for forthcoming analyses of the luminosity step and the broader role of galaxy environment in SN~Ia standardization and cosmology.
entry.arxiv:comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 33 pages, 22 figures, 5 tables

entry.title: The Entangling of Supernova Feedback Impacts with Coarsening Simulation Resolution
entry.summary: It is often understood that supernova (SN) feedback in galaxies is responsible for regulating star formation (SF) and generating gaseous outflows. However, a detailed look at the small-scale effects of SNe on the interstellar medium (ISM) in simulations shows that the macroscopic processes of SF suppression and outflow generation proceed in distinct channels. We demonstrate this finding in two independent simulations of isolated dwarf galaxies with very high (m_gas ~ Msun) numerical resolution, LYRA and RIGEL. Our findings suggest that the macroscopic effect of a given SN on the galaxy is best predicted by its local density. Outflows are primarily linked to SNe in diffuse regions expanding to their cooling radii on large (~kpc) scales, while dense SF regions are disrupted in a localized (~pc) manner. However, these separate feedback channels are only distinguishable at very high resolutions capable of following mass scales \lesssim 10^2 \msun. When averaging on coarser scales, ISM densities are greatly mis-estimated, and variations between different SF and SNe-affected regions are severely washed out. It therefore cannot be __self-consistently__ determined, from coarse-resolution information __alone__, (1) whether a SN tends to contribute to outflows or direct SF suppression, and (2) the rate of SF in a given region. In particular, commonly used parameters in coarse-resolution (subgrid) models, such as the SN cooling radius and SF density threshold, may require more detailed treatments informed by high-resolution studies.
entry.arxiv:comment: Published in the Open Journal of Astrophysics. 11 pages (excluding bibliography), 7 figures; comments welcome

entry.title: The KLN theorem meets collinear factorisation: Local Unitarity for hadronic cross-sections
entry.summary: We present an initial-state implementation of the Kinoshita-Lee-Nauenberg (KLN) theorem that is compatible with collinear factorisation. In this formulation, hadronic cross-sections are expressed as convolutions of parton distribution functions with partonic cross-sections obtained by summing over the number of incoming partons. By virtue of the KLN theorem, the partonic cross-sections are infrared finite by construction, without relying on dimensional regularisation as an infrared regulator. The Local Unitarity formalism provides a local realisation of this infrared finiteness, allowing partonic cross-sections to be evaluated directly in four dimensions by Monte Carlo integration. We demonstrate the framework at next-to-leading order and leading power. Using Local Unitarity, we compute the Drell-Yan and $t\bar{t}$ production cross-sections numerically; using Reverse Unitarity, we obtain the deep inelastic scattering and Drell-Yan cross-sections analytically. In all cases, a universal scheme conversion relates our results to those obtained in the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ parton model.

entry.title: Depletion of Dark Matter Spikes by Massive Black Hole Mergers
entry.summary: Dark matter over-densities around massive black holes, known as dark matter spikes, can dephase gravitational waves emitted by intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs/EMRIs), offering a promising way to indirectly detect dark matter. This detection channel, however, requires the spike to survive over cosmological time-scales. We investigate the impact that a host black hole's merger history has on its dark-matter spike. We focus on how the inspiral of a massive-black-hole (MBH) binary modifies and disrupts these spikes within the central $\sim 100$ Schwarzschild radii of the black hole. We find that a single merger with mass ratio $q = 0.03$ is capable of reducing a spike's density by around 3 (5) orders of magnitude at 100 (5) Schwarzschild radii across all polar angles relative to the binary's plane, independent of the primary MBH's mass, with larger mass ratios inducing even stronger depletion. In fact, a single past merger with mass ratio as small as $q = 0.005$ reduces central densities by 2--3 orders of magnitude, making gravitational-wave dephasing difficult to detect. We relate these results to the MBH merger history by analysing cosmological simulation data from Horizon-AGN. We find that mergers become increasingly common as the MBH mass increases, with mergers of mass ratio q > 0.03 having occurred in 50% of MBHs of mass $3\times10^7M_\odot$ and 95% of mass $10^8M_\odot$ at z=0. These fractions are reached at even lighter masses ($2\times10^7M_\odot$ and $5\times10^7M_\odot$, respectively) at z=3. We find that accretion-induced adiabatic MBH growth is unable to cause appreciable spike re-growth between such mergers in {\tt Horizon-AGN}. Thus, in combination with previous studies of EMRI-induced depletion, this work constrains the mass range over which massive black holes can host detectable DM spikes to $10^6M_\odot$--$5 \times 10^7M_\odot$ for $z \leq 3$.

entry.title: Study of the frustrated SU(3) Heisenberg chain with SU(3)-symmetric matrix product states
entry.summary: We study the SU(3) Heisenberg chain with nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange $J_1$ and $J_2$. Field theory predicts that the trimerized valence-bond solid of this chain has a finite extent in $α=J_2/J_1$, followed by a gapless SU(3)$_1$ phase, but earlier numerical estimates of the upper boundary range from $α\approx2.1$ (exact diagonalization) to $α\approx3.8$ (iDMRG). We use the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) algorithm with the full non-Abelian SU(3) symmetry imposed on the virtual bonds, reaching bond dimensions up to $D\approx8000$, and locate the phase boundaries by finite-entanglement scaling. Resolving the transfer-matrix spectrum and the entanglement spectrum by SU(3) irreducible representation, we find that the trimerized phase extends to $α_{c2}\gtrsim3.5$ and end below $α\approx5$, excluding a boundary near $α\approx2$. At larger $α$ our numerical analysis of the effective central charge is consistent with the predicted massless flow from SU(3)$_2$ to SU(3)$_1$.

entry.title: Quantum fields in a cold atomic simulator: relaxation and phase locking in tunnel-coupled 1D bosonic quasi-condensates
entry.summary: We consider a prime example of simulating interacting relativistic QFT with cold atoms: the realisation of the sine-Gordon model by tunnel-coupled quasi-1D Bose gases. While experiments have shown that it can realise the sine-Gordon model in equilibrium, studies of non-equilibrium dynamics have revealed phase-locking behaviour that contrasts with predictions from sine-Gordon field theory. Here, we examine a one-dimensional field-theoretic model of the system and find that the phase-locking behaviour can be understood in terms of the longitudinal harmonic trap, and that the additional degrees of freedom observed in the experiment do not appear to play a significant role. Therefore, the experimental setup provides a good simulator of the sine-Gordon quantum field theory, even out of equilibrium, if the inhomogeneous background induced by the trap is taken into account. Furthermore, our results support the idea that modifying the longitudinal trap to a box shape should result in agreement with standard sine-Gordon dynamics. The main remaining open issues are accounting for 3D corrections and modelling the effect of the boundaries.
